caseno: Death Reference No. 47 of 2010 with Criminal Appeal No. 4387 of 2010 with Jail Appeal No. 235 of 2010.
lawyer:
MA Mannan Mohon, DAG with Md. Aminur Rahman Chowdhury and Kazi Bazlur Rashid, AAGs—For the State. 
Md. Shamsuddin Babul, with Md. Lokman Hossain, Advocates—For the Condemned-Prisoner
Hasna Begum, Advocate—For the State Defence.
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
vs
Abdul Wadud Mithu and anothers ----- Condemned-Prisoner
full_judgment: 44. Mr Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the condemned-prisoner submits that the learned trial court during disposal of the original case committed gross illegality and irregularity and failed to assess the evidence on record in its true perspective. The learned Advocate further submits that the date of occurrence was 13-1-2009 at about 8-30 am as stated in the ejahar but the ejahar after a considerable time was lodged at 4-25 pm. The weapon which was used allegedly in the occurrence of killing the victim boy Zihad was a sharp cutting 'dao' which was recovered from a graveyard but it has come to the notice of the court that after the occurrence the condemned-prisoner Abdul Wadud Mithu ran away from the place of occurrence with that 'dao'. The learned trial court in this context has failed to appreciate the factual aspects of the case and failed to appreciate the law as well as the deposition of the eye-witnesses of the occurrence PWs 2 and 3. The learned Advocate further submits that admittedly there was enmity between the parties and the informant during his testimony as PW 1 stated that in the year 2006 he filed a criminal case against the condemned-prisoner Mithu and that case was GR 501 of 2006. For the reason stated above it was very much likely for the informant to implicate the condemned-prisoner Abdul Wadud Milieu with this case falsely. Besides this; the ocular witnesses of this case PW 2 Abul Bashar and PW 3 Parveen Akter are closely related with the informant and as they are related with the informant party; they deposed falsely implicating the condemned-prisoner with the occurrence. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court during disposal of the original Sessions case failed to consider the facts and circumstances of the case that the accused-appellant Abdul Wadud Mithu and the informant are of the same homestead and inasmuch as the victim's family members are in possession of some landed property on which the appellant had legal claim, the allegation against the accused-appellant viz the condemned-prisoner Abdul Wadud Mithu is false, baseless and fabricated. Neither any occurrence as alleged in the FIR was took place nor the accused-appellant was involved therein in any way and the victim boy may have killed by some other assailants and the informant taking advantage of death of Zihad in connivance with his relations and the police, has falsely implicated the name of the condemned-prisoner with the aforesaid death of the victim boy. The learned Advocate further submits that the prosecution during trial of the original case completely failed to prove that the condemned-prisoner was involved in the alleged offence but being guided by sentiment the learned trial court passed the order of conviction and sentence which is not tenable in the eye of law. In absence credible witnesses in the trial the conviction and sentence is based upon the statement of hearsay witnesses which is unwarranted. The learned Sessions Judge, Noakhali did not make any specific findings based on materials on record and discussed anything as to the involvement of the condemned-prisoner with the alleged offence and thus the learned trial court erred in law in disposing the original case. The learned Advocate argued that the condemned-prisoner was all along absent in the alleged place of occurrence at the time as stated from the side of the prosecution and with an ulterior motive the case was made out subsequently by the local police. The learned trial court also failed to assess properly and sufficiently the elements and ingredients of the offence as alleged against the condemned-prisoner and the burden of proof which was entirely on the prosecution and the eye-witnesses of the case in fact not properly cross-examined from the side of the defence and the defence during trial of the original case not at all obtained any opportunity to press their case and falsify the prosecution story. In support of this submission the learned Advocate has drawn our attention on the order-sheets of the learned trial court especially the order No. 2 dated 30-6-2009. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the ocular witnesses No. 2 and 3 stated a different story with that of their statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by a Magistrate, 1st Class but the learned trial court without proper sifting of evidence and assessment of the same decided the merit of the case in favour of the prosecution arbitrarily and the aforesaid two ocular witnesses are not trustworthy rather they were highly interested in favour of the prosecution and there is no satisfactory explanation from the side of the witness No. 2 of the prosecution as to how he went to the place of occurrence and why the local Member of Parliament with the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station appeared in the place of occurrence immediately after the occurrence of killing the victim boy Zihad and this very fact and circumstances has cast a serious doubt which is totally ignored by the learned trial Judge and the examination of the condemned-prisoner under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was defective and not proper and as a result of that the condemned-prisoner is liable to acquitted.
